entries.name: Band External Rotation
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository as the shoulder-rotation family base: standing side-on with the elbow pinned at the ribs (exact shoulder circle) and the forearm sweeping the rotation arc from across the body to forward; the band runs from an elbow-height anchor to the hand and visibly changes length through the rotation. The camera is now front, which is the fix this movement needed: from the side the forearm's rotation is mostly into or out of the screen - the hand travelled 10.2 units while the elbow never moved off its mark, so the articulation the movement is named for was the one thing the side view hid. From the front the sweep is in the plane of the picture. The upper arm hangs at the side, the elbow is anchored for the whole rep as the instructions ask, and the forearm rotates out from across the body, up to vertical. The hand is stepped round the arc in 22.5 degree increments so the eased in-between frames keep the forearm at its full 12.0 length. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Ten drawn positions of a band external rotation, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Forearm across the body, elbow tucked at the side.
Start rotating the forearm out, elbow anchored.
Quarter turn out, the elbow still fixed.
Continue out; the shoulder is doing the work.
Forearm down in front of the hip, elbow still anchored.
Hold the bottom of the rotation.
Rotate back in under control.
Quarter turn back toward the body.
Ease the forearm back across.
Back to the start position.

entries.name: Cable Internal Rotation
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed the free arm mirroring the working one. Source-bound front-view draft: the cable is out to the working side at elbow height; the working upper arm hangs still at the side with the elbow at a right angle, and the level forearm turns from pointing at the cable to the centreline, pauses, and returns. The free arm hangs still. The cable only lengthens as the forearm turns in.
entries.summary: Side-on to a cable at elbow height with the elbow bent ninety degrees at your ribs, rotate the forearm across the torso to the centreline, pause, then return until it points at the cable.

frames.caption: Set a single cable handle around elbow height and stand side-on with the working elbow bent to 90 degrees and resting lightly against the ribs.
Rotate the forearm across the torso while the upper arm stays quiet.
Pause when the hand reaches the centreline.
Return until the forearm points toward the cable.
Rotate around a quiet upper arm.

entries.name: Internal Rotation with Band
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed the free arm mirroring the working one. Source-bound front-view draft: a band fixed out to the working side at elbow height; the near upper arm stays at the side with the elbow at a right angle, and the level forearm turns from pointing out at the band to across the body, pauses, and returns more slowly. The free arm hangs still. One side is shown; the last caption carries the change of sides.
entries.summary: Side-on to a band at elbow height with the near elbow pinned to your side, rotate the forearm in across the body as far as you can, pause, return slowly, then change sides.

frames.caption: Fix a band at elbow height, stand side-on to it with the near elbow pressed to your side and bent to a right angle, the forearm pointing out away from the body.
Keeping the elbow at your side, rotate the forearm in across the body as far as you can.
Pause. Elbow stays pinned to the side.
Let it return slowly to the start.
Complete the repetitions, then change sides.
